bridge_feasible.observed:
PREDICTION REFUTED, in two dispatches, and the split is the finding.

FIRST DISPATCH -- verdict confirmed against the tool as it stood, basis refuted. `vit interface` emitted `INTEGER(C_INT), INTENT(INOUT) :: list(*)` plus `INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: n_list`, under a wrapper declaring `INTEGER(4), INTENT(INOUT) :: list(:)` -- the ALLOCATABLE attribute dropped with no diagnostic, although fortran_parser had recorded is_allocatable=True. Measured against the original on the live ROSCO path (allocate 4, append 3x): the caller's array was still 4 elements, the appended values written one past the end of its heap block, and nothing -- gfortran, g++, or the run -- said so. A hand-written Fortran 2018 CFI bridge reproduced the oracle BYTE FOR BYTE on both branches, so the limit was VIT's, not the argument's. evidence/AddToList/bridge_probe/result.json.

SECOND DISPATCH -- the verdict is refuted too. VIT 37f8bdf generates that bridge: the dummy is declared in the BIND(C) interface exactly as the original declares it (`DIMENSION(:), ALLOCATABLE, INTENT(INOUT)`), no extent parameter is emitted, and the C side receives the caller's own CFI_cdesc_t*. The unit is INTEGRATED on that path. Nothing about it is hand-written: interface block, wrapper, C++ scaffold, the differential harness's Fortran bridge and the post-integration shim are all generated (X1, X2). The loop's harness learned the same convention (cf885e3) -- three generators, which is what the escalation said it would take.

WHERE THE BASIS CAME FROM: tests/conformance/matrix.toml's `[c_alloc_inout] compiles = "no"` was measured from `test_validate.generate_fortran_bridge` -- the DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS's Fortran side, never linked into the library -- while `vit integrate` ships `interface_gen`'s output, which compiled clean and did nothing. The cell now reads compiles="yes", integrates="yes", re-measured. The prediction was right by luck of a different generator failing.

STILL REFUSED by VIT, for being UNMEASURED rather than impossible, each with its reason in the exception message: a SCALAR allocatable, rank >= 2, a CHARACTER or derived-type element, and any type/kind the interface cannot declare as the actual's own (LOGICAL, COMPLEX). The three other `bridge_feasible: no` entries waiting on this -- Read_OL_Input, ParseInAry_Opt, ParseDbAry_Opt -- are not thereby unblocked: their verdicts were derived from the same pre-`integrates` matrix and have to be re-measured, not inferred from this one.

units.observability:
THE GATE CANNOT SEE THIS UNIT, AND NOT BECAUSE THE CODE IS DEAD. `Conv2UC` runs 1,333,146 times across the 27 scenarios and converts 4,558,823 characters -- among the hottest procedures in the controller (coverage/line_coverage.json, clean lines 1579/1595). Both artifacts record replacements: 1, perturbed: true, reverted: true, revert_verified: true, so the perturbed library was genuinely built and run. gate/Conv2UC.redtest.json and evidence/Conv2UC/gate_redtests/.

The cause is structural. Every value this unit produces is consumed by an equality test against ANOTHER of its own outputs: FindLine converts the expected parameter name (ROSCO_Helpers.f90:1106) and the file's word (1118) with the same function and compares them. A perturbation applied to both operands preserves equality, and the no-conversion run shows equality survives even the non-injective case on the inputs these scenarios carry. So gate/Conv2UC.json -- 5,252,000 values compared, 0 mismatched -- is a green that constrains nothing about Conv2UC, and is committed next to the red tests that say why.

This is a THIRD shape of P9 in four units, and the sharpest: #1 was a line no scenario reached, #3 was an argument constant in every scenario, and this is an executed line whose result is cancelled downstream. A hit count of 1.3M says nothing about observability.

WHAT DOES CONSTRAIN IT, all red-tested:

The window is alive and TWO instruments say so: decoding the state files shows 31 of the 63 captured strings actually change, and a no-op stub scores exactly 31 OUT_TOL. For a CHARACTER field a kernel PASS *is* a bit-identity claim -- KGen's generated comparison has no tolerance branch at all, which is the per-TYPE counterpart to unit #3's finding rather than a contradiction of it.
  * 118 differential cases against the clean Fortran, 0 failed; the no-op stub turns 27 of them red. Strings at lengths 1/3/8 in three shapes (mixed, word-then-blanks, all-blank) over a 22-character corpus built from the reference's own 'a' and 'z' plus their collating neighbours.

bridge_feasible.observed:
PREDICTION NOW RESOLVED FOR THE INTEGRATION PATH. The first dispatch recorded that VIT REFUSES to generate anything for this unit, deterministically, because TYPE(ErrorVariables) carries `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE :: ErrMsg`. That refusal was correct and is now CLOSED, in VIT (a2e2c30), additively and red-tested.

A deferred-length CHARACTER has no C type, because its LENGTH is part of its allocation: reassigning it reallocates it, and C++ cannot reallocate Fortran's storage. It therefore crosses as THREE members -- a staging buffer the populator module owns, the current length, and the writable CAPACITY -- with the reallocating assignment performed by the reverse copy. The capacity is the member that makes the field writable rather than merely readable; without it the C++ cannot know how much room it has and `ErrVar%ErrMsg = RoutineName//':'//TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg)` could not be translated at all. Over-long assignment is REFUSED and reported, never truncated: a shortened error message is a plausible wrong answer, the one kind a bit comparison cannot catch.

`vit analyze-types --fix character`, the remedy VIT's own message suggested, is still REFUSED and now unnecessary. It rewrites ROSCO's type definition to a fixed length, changing LEN(ErrVar%ErrMsg), which sizes avcMSG, which is Record 49. P7.

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX: `vit translate ExtController` succeeds; `vit interface` emits all five arguments over a five-argument bridge -- read attribute by attribute against the original and matching, including REAL(4) for REAL(ReKi) (an explicit kind is not promoted by -fdefault-real-8). Generated view populators are committed at rosco/controller/src/vit_{controlparameters,localvariables,extcontroltype,errorvariables}_view.f90 and compile.

A SECOND VIT DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY, RECORDED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED (C12), and much larger than this unit. `vit test-validate` emitted the differential bridge's dummy list on ONE LINE. Decomposing ControlParameters (214 fields) and LocalVariables (168) produced a SUBROUTINE statement 11,747 characters long; free-form Fortran's limit is 132 columns, so gfortran truncated it and reported 1,153 diagnostics, none of which named the cause. EVERY unit in this campaign taking either type -- most of ROSCO's controllers -- was outside `vit test-validate` entirely, and nothing said so. The campaign's first four units took scalars, arrays and strings and never touched a derived type, which is why it went unmeasured until here. Fixed in VIT (83d25f9) as a rule about line CONTENTS rather than a list of emission sites, because wrapping only the dummy list left the array copy-in statements at 133-153 columns. statemachine_bridge.f90 now compiles; the wrong artifact is kept at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/.

STILL REFUSED, and this is what now blocks the unit: a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a DECOMPOSED derived type, in `vit test-validate`. `_decomposed_param_names` classifies on is_allocatable first, so ErrMsg is routed to the array path and `get_type_mapping` raises. The fix is the same three-member shape already built for the view struct, one generator over.

SECOND BRIDGE, STILL NOT MEASURED: plan.json declares LoadDynamicLib a permanent bridge, and ExtController's SAVE local `DLL_Ext` is a TYPE(ExtDLL_Type) -- five fields including TYPE(C_FUNPTR) :: ProcAddr(3) and CHARACTER(1024) :: ProcName(3). It does not cross the signature, so it needs a production bridge that owns the SAVE state, not a view. X1 forbids inlining LoadDynamicLib to avoid it.

RESOLVED FOR THE DIFFERENTIAL PATH TOO, in VIT 8c34ceb. The refusal recorded above -- a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a decomposed type -- is closed, as buffer + length + capacity, the same three members the view struct already used. Three more shapes had to change with it, and two of them were silent rather than refusing: a rank-1 ALLOCATABLE field and a SCALAR field of an INOUT argument were both INPUT-ONLY (no copy-back at all), and a LOGICAL field crossed as int32_t on one side and int8_t on the other. See `escalation`.

The ExtDLL_Type production bridge is BUILT: rosco/controller/src/vit_extcontroller_dll.f90 owns the SAVE TYPE(ExtDLL_Type), calls LoadDynamicLib (X1 -- it is called, not reproduced) and returns ProcAddr(1) as a C function pointer for the translation to call through, which is what C_F_PROCPOINTER compiles to. `ALLOCATE(ExtDLL%avrSWAP(max_avr_entries))` is NOT auto-extracted: vit/allocate_extract.py classifies it `local` because the size is a local PARAMETER, and `--auto-allocate`'s output does not compile on this codebase at all. See `escalation`.

units.observability:
THE GATE STILL CANNOT SEE THIS UNIT, AND THAT IS UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING.

ExtControl.f90 measures 0 of 28 EXECUTABLE lines in all 27 scenarios (evidence/ExtController/coverage_extcontrol.json prints 0/28 twenty-seven times; the denominator had to be regenerated because coverage/line_coverage.json stores only non-zero hit counts, so 'never ran' and 'never instrumented' are the same empty dictionary). Re-measured against the INTEGRATED Release build: making the unit a no-op moved 0 of 5,252,000 values, replacements: 1, revert_verified: true, residual_dirt: []. gate/ExtController.json's green constrains nothing and is committed beside gate/ExtController.redtest.json, which says so.

Nothing about that changes with the oracle fixture. DISCON.F90's own comment says it: 'Data from external dll is in ExtDLL%avrSWAP, it's unused in the following code'. Even a working external controller writes nothing the gate compares.

WHAT THE HARNESS CAN AND CANNOT SEE, stated rather than left to be found:
  SEEN   ExtDLL%avrSWAP (2000 elements and the extent itself), ErrVar%ErrStat, ErrVar%ErrMsg and its length, and every one of CntrPar's 286 decomposed parameters -- 448 compared outputs per case. The three length records the unit computes are read back by the oracle, and so are the bytes of accINFILE and avcOUTNAME and the incoming aviFAIL, because the fixture was extended to fold them in when it turned out they were reaching the library and never being read.
  NOT SEEN  (1) The `iStatus /= 0` path. harness/ranges.toml pins iStatus to 0, so the initialisation branch runs on every case and its ABSENCE is never exercised. The four statements it skips are the two DLL_Ext assignments, LoadDynamicLib, the ALLOCATE and four PRINTs; everything after END IF runs identically on both paths.
  (2) DLL_FileName and DLL_ProcName are held at one value each, so nothing here distinguishes a translation that reads them from one that ignores them. DLL_InFile is NOT pinned and is built by the same TRIM/TRANSFER shape, which is what keeps that code observable.
  (3) LEN_TRIM(ErrVar%ErrMsg) is 0 in every admissible case, because LoadDynamicLib blank-fills the message through a CHARACTER(*), INTENT(OUT) dummy. Two of the four declared-equivalent mutants are that.
  (4) LocalVar%ACC_INFILE is a CHARACTER ARRAY field, which the harness refuses rather than flattening; it is supplied as a zeroed buffer and not compared. This unit does not read it.

So the shape of the answer is unit #1's, one instrument further along: a DEAD unit closes on the harness and the mutation score, and the gate's green for it is evidence of nothing and is committed as such.
units.escalation:
CLOSED. All three remaining items are done, and the disposition is now `integrated`.

  A. `vit test-validate` crossing a deferred-length CHARACTER FIELD of a decomposed type -- DONE, VIT 8c34ceb, as buffer + length + capacity, the same three members a2e2c30 built for the view struct. This was the 37-of-69 blocker.
  B. The loop harness supplying CHARACTER fields -- DONE, loop 7d7c913. Both shapes cross (fixed-width and deferred-length); a CHARACTER ARRAY field is still refused, with its reason.
  C. The JUDGEMENT about what the harness may hold constant -- MADE, and written down where it can be reviewed: harness/ranges.toml, which is committed and states the measurement forcing each of its four pins. Every one exists because the REFERENCE crashes on the rest of the domain, not because the translation would: ExtController never checks ErrVar%ErrStat after LoadDynamicLib and calls through a null ProcAddr. That is a finding about upstream ROSCO and the file says so.

A FOURTH THING WAS FOUND ON THE WAY AND IS LARGER THAN ANY OF THEM (C12). The decomposed bridge copied every field IN and almost none OUT: a rank-1 ALLOCATABLE field and a SCALAR field of an INOUT argument were both input-only, so ExtDLL%avrSWAP -- this unit's principal output -- and ErrVar%ErrStat were supplied to the reference and then discarded. Every unit in this campaign taking a derived type was affected. The wrong artifact is kept at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/extcontroller_bridge.alloc_input_only.f90.

STILL OPEN, and now the campaign's problem rather than this unit's: `vit integrate --auto-allocate` cannot be used on this codebase. Three defects, measured, artifact at evidence/ExtController/vit_defects/integrate_auto_allocate.wrapper.f90 -- its copy-call scan matches ANY `CALL x(..., arg%field, ...)` and hoisted BOTH LoadDynamicLib and the external DLL call into the wrapper; it declines a size expression that is a local PARAMETER; and its error handling emits SetErrStat and CHARACTER(ErrMsgLen), OpenFAST names that exist nowhere in ROSCO. The one ALLOCATE this unit needs is therefore in the committed wrapper with the reason beside it.

units.observability:
THE GATE IS BLIND TO THIS UNIT FOR TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS, AND THE SECOND IS A FIFTH SHAPE OF P9. Making the unit return XXXXXXXX moved 0 of 5,252,000 values.

1. THE EXERCISED DOMAIN IS THE IDENTITY. Every scenario's avcOUTNAME is `vit_sim<N>`, which contains no '.', so all 444,000 calls take the same one of the procedure's five leaves. Coverage says it exactly: clean ROSCO_Helpers.f90:1280 `IF (GivenFil(I:I) == '.')` is evaluated 4,304,000 times and EVERY assignment inside it -- lines 1283, 1284, 1285, 1287, 1290 -- has ZERO hits in all 27 scenarios, as does the special case at 1270. Only the fall-through at 1302 runs. A no-op is therefore the CORRECT answer on the whole exercised domain, which is why the campaign's standard no-op gate red test is degenerate here.

2. THE RESULT IS CONSUMED, AND THE CONSUMPTION IS A SIDE EFFECT THE GATE DOES NOT MEASURE. RootName has six reader sites, all of them building a FILENAME. Five are dead in all 27 (ROSCO_IO.f90:1110, 1142, 30, 373 and ReadSetParameters.f90:360 -- 0 hits each). The sixth, ROSCO_IO.f90:1102, runs 24 times across 23 scenarios and is `OPEN(unit=UnDb, FILE=TRIM(RootName)//'.RO.dbg')`. The gate compares baseline_arrays/scenario_N.npz, built by Examples/vit_sim.py from the arrays crossing the DLL boundary; it never opens a .RO.dbg. Perturbing this unit renames a file.

That is distinct from the four shapes already recorded -- unexercised line (#1), argument constant in every scenario (#3), result cancelled downstream (#4), result produced and never consumed (#6). Here the result IS consumed, by a live line, into a channel outside the instrument. coverage/line_coverage.json can express none of the five; ROSCO_IO.f90:1102 is hit in nearly every scenario.

THE KERNEL IS A MIRROR, not merely a lookup table. The call site aliases the INTENT(IN) and INTENT(OUT) dummies, so the captured input equals the captured expected output and a NO-OP passes 62/62 IDENTICAL. Whenever a call site aliases in that way, the no-op stub stops being a liveness test for the kernel and becomes a vacuity test; the liveness test has to be a WRONG-constant stub. Both artifacts are committed.

COST, STATED, and it is unit #6's defect again: `vit interface` emits a copy-IN for RootName, an INTENT(OUT) dummy. It does not change this unit's answer, because the translation writes every one of len_RootName bytes -- but it is why 26 of 726 differential cases survive the no-op red test, and it would mask a translation that failed to write the tail. Left in the generated wrapper with the defect recorded in STATUS.md rather than hand-edited. Note that at THIS call site the copy-in is not even a read of undefined storage, because the aliased GivenFil has defined it.

WHAT THE DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS COST TO MAKE HONEST. Its first green -- 224 checked, 0 failed -- covered no case in which a '.' was followed by an ordinary character, i.e. no case of stripping an extension. The generator could not build one: the corpus is the reference's literals plus their COLLATING NEIGHBOURS, and '/' is '.'+1, so a corpus laid down in order always puts a separator after the dot. That is a general statement about R6, not about GetRoot, and it is written into harness/generate.py where the next unit will meet it.
